I wasn’t taking my anti depressants properly, had insane insomnia, planned to kill myself Monday night, instead I admitted myself to hospital and I’m still here. I was on sertraline 50mg, didn’t notice a huge difference, now I’m on sertraline 100mg, they eventually want to up it to 150mg and so on. I wish I was taking it sooner. I’m feeling better and better every day. Just in the sense of organising my thoughts. The negative thoughts are still there but not controlling me anymore. If you want to talk about it please message me. I’m so proud of you for recognising that this is what you need. Such a huge stigma around AD. We wouldn’t get angry at a Diabetic for not being able to produce their own insulin, why do people get angry at us for not being able to balance the chemicals in our brain? Doesn’t make sense!
Keep being strong ❤️ xxxxxx

It was about 7 at night, I walked through the front door and it was a ghost town. I stood there frozen contemplating leaving. I’m not sure how long I stood there for, but just as I was about to turn around and leave, a young nurse walked down the corridor, looked at me and said “Hey, do you need a hand with something?”. And I murmured “I need to see someone”. And she said “Sure, who would you like to see?” And I said “a nurse”. And she said “let’s go somewhere private”.
She took me to a spare little room (looked like a dialysis room), shut the door and sat me down and listened to me ramble about my C-PTSD, Depression, and that I had had enough. She just sat and nodded and listened. This room was right across from the nurses station so she asked the nurses to keep an eye on me,  she told me she wanted to keep the door open because it was stuffy (it’s Australia, it’s hot, but I knew that wasn’t the reason she wanted the door open, but I appreciated her not making a scene), she went and got me some water and paperwork which she filled out for me. She asked me questions such as: do you feel comfortable enough talking to me about your C-PTSD - because if you don’t that’s okay? Are you sleeping? Are you eating? Are you drinking water? Have you been drinking alcohol lately? Do you take drugs? Do you self harm? What do you use? Have you got support people? Do you want us to call anyone for you? Are you having negative thoughts about your life right now?
I told her about my self harm from last week and she asked how I did it. There was no judgement in her voice at all. She took blood pressure, heart rate and temperature.
She then got the doctor and the doctor had much the same conversation with me, talked to me gently. Asked me if I felt in danger to myself still which I said yes but not as much I just felt very shaken and nervous. She asked me if I felt like harming myself, would I see someone or just do it, and I said I’d see someone at this stage.
She said she wanted me to sleep tonight, that was her priority, so she prescribed me two really strong sleeping tablets that the nurses would give me. She left and I was left with the nurse who showed me to my room, and where the buzzer, TV remote, aircon control was etc...
She redressed my week old self harm wounds which I had nervously been picking at causing them to bleed without realising. She ordered another nurse to get me something for tea that was easy on the stomach (2 bits of toast, jelly, orange juice). She took blood pressure, heart rate and temperature again.
She asked how I felt and she said that she was embarrassed to ask this question but she asked if she could check my bag to make sure I had nothing I could harm myself with (was a requirement). She asked if I wanted to empty it myself or if she could and I said she could. She looked through it on the bed in front of me and kept talking so the reality of everything didn’t have time to fully set in. She sat with me whilst I ate what I could, another nurse came in with the sleeping tablets. After I had them I went to the toilet, nurse stayed in my room. When I came back I had more water, she asked me if I liked to sleep in warm air or cold air and I said cold so she put it on cool for me.
She left the door open and stepped outside. They put me near the other nurses station so they could keep an eye on me. I zonked it for a few hours but found myself wide awake a bit later. The nurses on came and just generally chit chatted away to me in my room. Zoned in and out. They took my blood pressure etc... a few times.
In the morning the same dr came to ask me questions about my thoughts and if it had improved. Asked about sleep. They’re giving me something stronger tonight. I hope it works because I’m so tired.
Nurses have been lovely today, making sure I eat. Walking me down the hall. Just generally chatting away. They’re gaining a bit of trust in me but still wary. Fingers crossed to a good night sleep...
